page: Amazon Web Services x2gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Nitro architecture and 32 dedicated arm64 cores based on the AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. With one thread per physical core, it eliminates hyperthreading contention across its compute resources. The configuration pairs these 32 cores with 512 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 16 GB of RAM per core. Hardware acceleration includes integrated AES cryptography instructions, though x86-specific vector instruction sets like AVX-512 are not present.

For fast local data persistence and caching, the instance bundles 1900 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage. The network interface supports a baseline throughput of 12 Gbps. In benchmark tests, the instance shows reliable multi-core throughput, posting average tier results in stress-ng multi-core testing (48566.12) and Geekbench multi-core evaluation (11488.0). Memory throughput is stable under large workloads, measuring 139.81 GB/sec for uncached 256MB block reads and 70.12 GB/sec for uncached writes. Redis throughput reaches 36.44 million SET operations per second, complemented by a PassMark database score of 20286.9.

Performance profiles indicate notable tradeoffs between parallel scaling and single-core throughput. Single-threaded tasks place in lower percentiles, as demonstrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 942.0, a gzip compression rate of 20.31 GB/sec, and modest performance in lightweight LLM inference tasks. However, multi-threaded operations scale effectively across all 32 dedicated cores without simultaneous multithreading overhead.

The balance of massive memory density, dedicated physical cores, and high-speed local NVMe storage delivers strong qualitative cost efficiency for memory-bound applications. The x2gd.8xlarge is suited for in-memory databases like Redis and Memcached, large relational database engines requiring large buffer pools, real-time analytics, and heavy ETL pipelines optimized for the ARM64 ecosystem.
description: Amazon Web Services x2gd.8xlarge is a memory-optimized instance featuring 32 dedicated 64-bit ARM Neoverse-N1 cores clocked at 2.5 GHz with a 1:1 physical-to-virtual core allocation. Designed for high memory footprints, the platform provides 512 GB of RAM, offering 16 GB of memory per core alongside 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 12 Gbps baseline network throughput. Benchmark testing shows average multi-core execution capabilities, reaching 48566.12 in stress-ng multi-core and delivering 36.44 million Redis SET operations per second. However, single-threaded processing exhibits lower throughput, evidenced by a 942.0 single-core Geekbench score. Lacking hardware GPUs, it balances extensive memory bandwidth and local NVMe capacity to deliver efficient resource density. This server is appropriate for in-memory databases, large caching layers, relational database buffer pools, and ARM-native batch processing environments.
